sections.label: How it works
sections.claim: An export is saved as a job first, so a crash never loses it.
sections.lead: Two workers share the work. If one stops halfway, the other goes on from the last finished page.

risks.then: The file stays on the screen too, and the owner is told when an email bounces.

risks.name: A huge month runs too long
risks.then: The file splits into parts, so no single part takes more than a minute.

decided.why: A big month takes minutes, and a web request times out after one.

decided.what: No live sync with accounting tools this round
decided.why: A file covers every tool now. Sync waits until enough exports show which tools matter.
Long enough to download again after the books close, short enough to keep storage small.

decided.what: Columns follow each tool's own import page
decided.why: A file the tool imports as is beats a neat file someone must fix.

decided.what: The owner picks the day the email goes out
decided.why: Books close on different days, and a file that arrives early is incomplete.

findings.finding: Export as PDF runs inside the web request and times out at 300 invoices.
No record of who exported what, so a bookkeeper cannot find last month's file.

research.question: What does each accounting tool import?
research.answer: Xero and QuickBooks each publish a sample import file. Matching their columns exactly removes every manual fix we saw.

plan.summary: Nine pieces of work in four steps, shipped as four pull requests. Each is proven on the local stack and reviewed before the next step starts.
plan.start: Each step ends with proof a person can check: a test, a screenshot or a run log under its card. A step starts only when the one before it is proven.
